narration.text: Whisper and text-to-speech both work with language, but they solve opposite problems.

visual.subtitle: Audio to text, or text to audio?

narration.text: Whisper starts with recorded speech and predicts the words a person said. Its output is text, ready for search, subtitles, or analysis.

Think of the systems as arrows pointing in opposite directions. Audio enters Whisper and text comes out. Text enters a speech engine and audio comes out. Those labels make the direction easy to remember.

scenes.title: Choose by the input you have

narration.text: Whisper is useful when speech already exists: meeting notes, voice search, accessibility captions, and transcription. Text-to-speech is useful when written content needs a spoken form, such as screen readers, navigation, or narrated lessons.

The interface makes the distinction concrete. A transcription function accepts audio and returns text. A speech function accepts text and returns audio, so their input and output types reveal which direction they travel.

visual.code:
const words = await transcribe(audio);
const speech = await speak(words);

scenes.title: Match the tool to the direction

narration.text: Remember the direction: Whisper turns speech into text; text-to-speech turns text into speech. Choose the tool that matches the data you have and the result you need.

visual.subtitle: Whisper: speech → text. TTS: text → speech.
